title: Fruit Into Baskets
observed_problem_fact: A window over a row of trees may hold at most two fruit types, so every move needs the number of distinct types in the window
idea_used: The distinct count changes only when a type count goes from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0, so it is kept as one integer beside the counts
m3_applicability: Every owned write moves one group size; nonEmptyGroups changes only on that group's 0<->1 transitions, so isEmpty() and keySet().size() read one int
compatibility_limit: Only owned writes are counted; after getMap()/setMap() and in foreign subclasses the next query recounts

title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
observed_problem_fact: Counting windows with exactly K distinct values needs the distinct count of each window in constant time
idea_used: The distinct count is maintained per step instead of rescanning the window
m3_applicability: The logical key count (non-empty groups; empty groups left by sub-list writes excluded) is maintained; LogicalGroups.size(), keys().uniqueSet().size() and the asMap cursor quota read it
compatibility_limit: An emptied group kept attached by a sub-list view stays a private empty owner, not a key, as before

title: All O`one Data Structure
observed_problem_fact: Every operation including the aggregate queries must run in O(1)
idea_used: Aggregates follow the delta of each increment and decrement instead of being recomputed
m3_applicability: size() is the running sum of the size change measured around each owned write (group size before and after), bulk writes that fail part-way included
compatibility_limit: A write re-entered from a callback, a read during a write or a raw directory exposure voids the delta (epoch guard); the next query recounts once in O(#keys)

title: Java Dequeue
observed_problem_fact: Every window of fixed size needs its number of unique integers; a rescan per window is too slow
idea_used: A count map plus one unique counter updated when a count enters or leaves zero
m3_applicability: The same 0<->1 rule covers groups attached and detached by put, remove, removeMapping, clear, iterator removal and view writes
compatibility_limit: The counters are transient: the serialized form is unchanged and readObject recounts once
